items.title: Java4Shell: critical Java flaw opens Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and others to takeover
items.why: A bug in Java's fast Base64 decoder (OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, on newer Intel/AMD chips) can let attackers run code in apps like Jira and Jenkins. New tonight: CISA urged immediate patching; no attacks are reported yet.
items.action: Update Java to the November Oracle or OpenJDK release on servers running Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak or similar, and check vendor appliances that bundle Java.

items.title: Attackers exploit a critical Puppet flaw to take over server management systems
items.why: CISA added a Puppet Enterprise and Puppet Core remote code execution bug to its exploited list on Nov. 17. Fixes came out Nov. 3; risk is higher where the Puppet certificate authority signs requests without strong checks.
items.action: Update to Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 or 2023.8.13, or Puppet Core 9.1.3 or 8.22.2, and rotate credentials if a server may have been hit.

items.title: Microsoft's AI agent toolkit on PyPI was hijacked to steal cloud credentials
items.why: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of the agent-framework Python package, live for about 45 minutes on Nov. 17, ran a stealer that grabs Azure, GitHub and other keys and tokens. The package gets about 190,000 downloads a month.
items.action: Ask developers to check for agent-framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2, pin to 1.26.0, rebuild affected machines and rotate their cloud and code keys.

items.title: Google sees attackers' AI agents find and exploit web app flaws from patches on their own
items.why: Google's threat team found an AI framework that compares patched and unpatched code, then builds and runs working exploits with no human help. The gap between a patch and an attack keeps shrinking.
items.action: Apply security updates for internet-facing websites and apps within days, not weeks, and turn on automatic updates where your vendor offers them.

items.title: Russian hackers used one hacked Google Workspace to break into a second US firm
items.why: Google says the Cold Relic group got a Super Admin password, wore down the victim with MFA push prompts, then exported company data and used stolen identities to phish a second organization.
items.action: Put phishing-resistant MFA such as passkeys or security keys on Google Workspace admins, and review registered devices, backup codes and app grants.

items.title: Ukraine and FBI arrest suspects in a fake IT support ransomware gang tied to $40 million
items.why: Police arrested four suspected leaders of a group that used AI-voiced calls posing as IT support to get passwords or remote access, then stole data and encrypted systems. At least 28 companies, including US firms, paid ransoms.
items.action: Tell staff that real IT support will never call asking for passwords or to install remote tools; verify any such call by calling IT back on a known number.
